newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian beer stocks slide as drinking reduces.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian beer stocks slide as drinking reduces.

text.p: Brewery shares on the Nigerian stock exchange are tumbling because the appetite of Nigerians for beer is falling, dealers and analysts said on Thursday.
Leading brewers have seen their prices slide this year in a continuation of a trend that started in 1996.
Nigerian Breweries Plc, the largest brewing concern, and second-placed Guinness closed unchanged on Wednesday at 16.00 naira and 7.80 naira, well below their opening prices in January.
"Margins in the sector are declining seriously because people do not have the means to buy beer like before," said analyst Ayo Oluwole.
The two big brewers both suffered huge price drops last year but Nigerian Breweries rallied to 19.30 naira by year's end.
Others are faring much worse. Jos International Breweries announced on Wednesday a loss of 7.1 million naira in its financial results to end-1995.
Nigerian Breweries and Guinness, the most actively traded shares in the sector, posted improved profits in their financial statements but this has not stopped investors selling their stocks.
Since the nation's economy took a downturn 10 years ago, individual incomes have progressively shrunk, leaving little for non-essential things such as drinking, analysts said.
From near parity to the dollar in 1986, the national currency currently trades at 80 naira to the U.S. unit, with consequent deterioration in purchasing power.
"Beer is the last thing I will spend money on when I don't have enough money to eat," said Oluwole, adding that was why Nigerian Breweries had diversified into soft drinks bottling.
It gained the franchise from Cadbury last year to bottle and market the Schweppes range of soft drinks, a strategy dealers said would boost profits due to a jump in non-alcoholic drinks consumption.
Many operators also attribute the trend partly to a surge in activities of religious organisations which preach abstinence from alcohol.
But some share traders said the decision to diversify into lower-priced stocks could be responsible for the slide.
"Investors are looking for stable stocks now. The breweries sector is not stable yet although there are prospects they will recover in future," broker Chuks Ohanwusi of Networth Securities said.
Despite the slide, foreign shareholders have continued to consolidate their interest in the companies.
Early last month, Guinness Plc effectively gained majority control of the Nigerian company following the conversion last year of loan stock worth 426.8 million naira.
The conversion raised Guinness Plc's stake to 52 percent from the former 40 percent.
Also last year, Dutch brewer Heineken,the technical partner of Nigerian Breweries, hiked its equity holding to 28 percent from 13.4 percent.
